summary.para: Find user-managed service accounts with a query.
Get a paginated list of user-managed service accounts and their information. You can optionally filter the results with a query.
NOTE: Built-in service accounts are not stored in the security index, so this API never returns them. Use the get service accounts API to list them.

The starting document offset. It must not be negative. By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the from and size parameters. To page through more hits, use the search_after parameter.

A query to filter which service accounts to return. If the query parameter is missing, it is equivalent to a match_all query. The query supports a subset of query types, including match_all, bool, term, terms, match, ids, prefix, wildcard, exists, range, and simple_query_string. You can query the following information associated with a service account: username, roles, enabled, description, created_by.username, created_by.realm, created_by.realm_type, created_by.api_key.id, created_by.api_key.name, created_at, updated_by.username, updated_by.realm, updated_by.realm_type, updated_by.api_key.id, updated_by.api_key.name, and updated_at.
NOTE: The username of a service account is its namespace/service pair, so use a prefix query on username to select a namespace.

The number of hits to return. It must not be negative. By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the from and size parameters. To page through more hits, use the search_after parameter.
The sort definition. All the fields that you can query on, other than description, are eligible for sorting. In addition, sort can also be applied to the _doc field to sort by index order.

If true, each service account also includes the profile UIDs of the users who created and last replaced it, under the created_by_profile_uid and updated_by_profile_uid fields. A profile UID is included only for a user who has an activated user profile.
